A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, five figures, and Appendices A–K support reliable comparison despite pagination and typesetting differences.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical bounds and proofs, including its appendices. Experimental applications and results are attributed to prior work; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its added measurement-noise discussion does not report experiments, simulations, or data analysis.

M1.justification: The halving-tree, Von Neumann-tree, and matrix-completion constructions are unchanged. The added Corollary 4.3 states a guarantee without introducing a new learning procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or evaluation. The new laboratory-noise discussion introduces no actually evaluated task or scenario.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison methods are added, removed, or revised. The new discussion of Aaronson et al. (2018) concerns theoretical optimality.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols. Section 2.2 adds explicit loss formulas and clarifies general feedback, without introducing an evaluation or changing an experimental setting.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or empirical case studies appear in either version. The expanded measurement-noise discussion supplies motivation rather than additional analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical probability bounds and probabilistic constructions are retained.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical numerical results or qualitative experimental findings. The added mistake-bound statement is a formal corollary, assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 adds Corollary 4.3: an O(n/ε²) mistake bound with feedback accurate to ε/3, asserted to be almost asymptotically optimal even for pure states. This is presented as a consequence of retained Theorem 4.1; the existing theorem statements and appendix derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contributions, and conclusion retain the same pure-versus-mixed hardness claim and regret results for the standard, ε-realizable, and smoothed settings. Corollary 4.3 adds a supporting consequence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly connects smoothed analysis to control fluctuations, thermal drift, and calibration errors, interpreting them as stochastic measurement perturbations. The formal smoothness definition and the conclusion's open questions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: No implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data access instructions are added or removed. The constructive details in the appendix proofs are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Leibfried et al. (2003) to motivate measurement noise and explicitly relates Corollary 4.3 to the optimality of Aaronson et al. (2018). The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited rewrites in Sections 2.2 and 5.2, an added corollary passage, and author/header and reference-style edits. Section and appendix ordering is retained. Some cross-references now incorrectly call lemmas, definitions, or corollaries theorems.

P2.justification: All five figures are retained. Figure 3 now precedes Theorem 3.4, Figure 5's caption changes its cross-reference wording, and text and bibliography wrapping are revised. The overall single-column layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v3 makes a useful mistake-bound consequence explicit and clarifies arbitrary feedback in Section 2.2, improving explanatory completeness. These modest gains outweigh the new cross-reference errors, such as calling Lemma 3.5 a theorem. The central theorems and existing proofs remain unchanged.
